🇲🇽🌎 <u>Gorillaz frontman salutes Sheinbaum at Corona Capital</u>

In front of 72,000 people in Mexico City, Damon Albarn waved a Palestinian flag a fan handed him, then talked about the president who flew to the APEC summit in China in economy class: 21 hours on a commercial flight, with a stop in Tijuana.

"I love Mexico because you have a revolutionary spirit. It's an inspiring country. I don't know much about your president, but the fact that she traveled in economy class is something really important to me."

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>Francesca Albanese is coming to Mexico</u>

The UN Special Rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territories will speak at UNAM on November 30, in the Aula Magna of the Faculty of Philosophy and Letters, invited by BDS México and the Organization of Academics with Palestine.

This is the jurist Washington sanctioned for documenting the genocide in Gaza. Days ago in Madrid she said it plainly: "There is no good Israel outside the settlements." Mexico's largest public university is giving her the floor.
banner: ALBANESE TO SPEAK AT UNAM NOV 30

text: 📸 Supervisión de obra de la Universidad Nacional Rosario Castellanos — Zacatecas, 21 de noviembre de 2026

🇲🇽✊ "It is much better to encourage each and every student than to separate them into those who supposedly have talent and those who don't." "They criticize us because we give a scholarship to each and every student. They say the scholarship should be only for those with good grades." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Well-being Scholarships event, Villanueva, Zacatecas, Nov 21, 2026 As Mexico City's head of government, Sheinbaum replaced the "Talented Children" scholarship, which went only to students with a 9–10 average, with a small one for every primary and secondary student. A study two years later found more children getting better grades. This year the universal secondary scholarship (Beca "Rita Cetina") brought 400,000 more young people into high school, and Zacatecas is the first state where every university student gets the "Gertrudis Bocanegra" scholarship.
banner: WHY EVERY STUDENT GETS A SCHOLARSHIP

text: 🇲🇽🎨 "Always think of your homeland, and always think that the scholarship you study with, you owe to the people of Mexico." "If I was able to study all the way to a doctorate thanks to scholarships the people of Mexico gave me, what I want most is for young Mexicans to be able to keep studying." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Well-being Scholarships event, Villanueva, Zacatecas, Nov 21, 2026 Sheinbaum recalled that 40 years ago, as an undergraduate, she took part in the student movement against the privatization of UNAM, which kept tuition and enrollment fees from rising. "Now as President, what I wish for most is that all young Mexicans have a place in high school and a place in university, and that all of them can have a scholarship. And you know what? We are going to achieve it."
banner: "YOU OWE IT TO THE PEOPLE OF MEXICO"

🇲🇽🎨 "The education budget reached a historic figure: 1.3 trillion pesos." "There are many groups that don't like so many resources going to scholarships. It angers them that young people now have the chance to study, that they are not discriminated against, that they are not called 'ninis' as before." — Mario Delgado, Secretary of Public Education, Well-being Scholarships event, Villanueva, Zacatecas, Nov 21, 2026 The 2027 budget raises education spending by 11%. Scholarships go from 187 to 190 billion pesos. Delgado called reports of cuts "false": the Benito Juárez Well-being Universities rise from 3.105 to 3.205 billion pesos, more than double their 2024 budget. In Zacatecas, every public school student at every level now has a scholarship: 320,893 students and more than 2.142 billion pesos.

🇲🇽🎨 "It's because there aren't enough places. If you had a passing grade in high school, you have the right to a place at university." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Well-being Scholarships event, Villanueva, Zacatecas, Nov 21, 2026 Sheinbaum asked the students how many of every 10 classmates from high school got into university. They shouted 6, 10, 3, 5. "Do you think it's because they didn't pass the admission exam?" "Yes!" "No." Governor David Monreal estimates about 10,000 young people in Zacatecas are left out of university, so the Rosario Castellanos National University campus under construction there will be built for 10,000 students, "so that nobody is left without studying university." She toured the construction site after the event.
